architecture.mechanism: Cavitation erosion mitigation via flow separation control and pressure recovery optimization in blade trailing edge regions
architecture.intervention: Install trailing-edge vortex generators (TEVGs) or passive flow control devices (e.g., micro-ramps) at 82% of the blade chord length from the leading edge to suppress flow separation and reduce the low-pressure interference zone causing cavitation
architecture.expected_effect: Reduce cavitation erosion depth by ≥50% over 5 years, maintaining blade thickness and preserving hydraulic efficiency within 3% of rated 45 MW
architecture.falsification_test: Compare erosion depth measurements at the trailing edge (82% chord) after 24,000 operating hours with/without TEVGs installed, using ultrasonic thickness gauging and visual inspection
